title: Reel assembly + teacher critique
description: Produce picture, sound, and finishing segments in declared order, concatenate them without merging, and critique the assembled reel before it is shown.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: wf-film-02
  title: Reel assembly + teacher critique
  description: Produce picture, sound, and finishing segments in declared order, concatenate them without
    merging, and critique the assembled reel before it is shown.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: Assemble a review reel in sequence order, critique it as an audience would experience it,
    and gate the screening on the notes being addressed.
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 4
    onFailure: preserve-completed
    requireApprovalFor:
      - n-approval
  nodes:
    - id: n-intake
      kind: input
      name: Reel brief and available media
      summary: Reel brief and available media
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - text
        properties:
          text:
            type: string
            description: The requester's objective, source material, or instructions.
          workflowFields:
            type: object
            required:
              - sequence_list
              - available_media
              - review_audience
              - runtime_target
            properties:
              sequence_list: {}
              available_media: {}
              review_audience: {}
              runtime_target: {}
        x-ladder-input-mode: text
    - id: n-scope
      kind: transform
      name: Select the segments to produce
      summary: select the sequences to assemble, in reel order
      config:
        operation: select
        expression: select the sequences to assemble, in reel order
    - id: n-segment1
      kind: agent
      templateRef: film-02
      name: Picture segments and structure
      summary: 'Segment 1: picture segments and structure.'
      role: Editor working structure, pacing, and clarity in the cut.
      prompt: You are an Editorial Story Analyst. You assess a cut for structural clarity, escalation,
        and whether the audience has the information each scene assumes, and you propose specific structural
        changes with the footage they require. You distinguish a pacing problem from a story problem,
        because trimming a scene that is structurally necessary makes the cut faster and worse.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - writing-editing
          - teaching
          - domain-analysis
          - decision-analysis
        tools:
          - read
        connectors:
          - mcp:mam
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-segment2
      kind: agent
      templateRef: film-05
      name: Sound design and dialogue pass
      summary: 'Segment 2: sound design and dialogue pass.'
      role: Sound lead building design, dialogue clarity, and compliant mixes.
      prompt: You are a Sound Design & Mix Lead. You build the sound design around what the scene needs
        the audience to feel and hear, protect dialogue intelligibility, and mix to the loudness and dynamic-range
        specification of each delivery target. You flag where a mix that works in the room will fail on
        a phone speaker, because that is where most of the audience will meet it.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - audio-processing
          - domain-analysis
          - compliance-review
          - evaluation
          - data-engineering
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-segment3
      kind: agent
      templateRef: film-04
      name: Look and finishing pass
      summary: 'Segment 3: look and finishing pass.'
      role: Colourist working look, consistency, and deliverable compliance.
      prompt: You are a Colour & Finishing Specialist. You build a look that survives every delivery target,
        keep shot-to-shot and scene-to-scene continuity, and check the grade against the actual broadcast
        or streaming specification. You state where a creative choice violates a delivery limit rather
        than shipping it and waiting for QC to catch it.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - video-processing
          - design-review
          - release-engineering
          - domain-analysis
          - data-engineering
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-assemble
      kind: aggregator
      name: Assemble the reel in sequence order
      summary: Preserve segment order exactly; concatenation is ordered assembly, not a merge.
      config:
        aggregation: concat
    - id: n-critique
      kind: teacher
      inlineRole: true
      name: Teacher critique of the assembled draft
      summary: Critique feedback from a host-resolved teacher model.
      role: Host-resolved teacher model
      prompt: 'You are the critique teacher for this reel. Watch it as the review audience will: where
        does the story lose the viewer, where does sound or picture pull focus from what the scene needs,
        and where does a segment boundary show? Return specific critique per segment with the moment it
        occurs.'
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
      config:
        teacherModel: host:teacher-model
        feedbackMode: critique
    - id: n-quality
      kind: evaluate
      inlineRole: true
      name: Score the assembled result
      summary: Evaluate narrative clarity, technical consistency across segments, and runtime against
        target.
      role: Deterministic metric evaluator
      prompt: Evaluate the upstream result against narrative clarity, technical consistency across segments,
        and runtime against target. Return a score, pass/fail verdict, the evidence behind the verdict,
        remaining uncertainty, and the smallest corrective action. Do not claim programmatic measurement
        unless the host supplies the required tool.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - score
          - passed
          - reasons
        properties:
          score:
            type: number
          passed:
            type: boolean
          reasons:
            type: array
            items:
              type: string
      config:
        threshold: 0.8
    - id: n-accept
      kind: condition
      name: Meets the bar?
      summary: Route on quality.passed.
      config:
        expression: quality.passed
        branches:
          - label: Accept
            when: 'true'
          - label: Revise
            when: 'false'
    - id: n-revise
      kind: agent
      templateRef: film-01
      name: Address the notes on the weakest segments
      summary: Apply the teacher critique to the weakest segments.
      role: Post supervisor designing conform, review, and delivery pipelines that hold up under change.
      prompt: You are a Post Pipeline Supervisor. You design the path from camera original to deliverable
        with the colour pipeline, naming convention, versioning, and review cadence fixed before work
        starts, and you name the step where a late change becomes expensive. You keep the conform reproducible
        from the original media, because a pipeline that cannot be re-run from source turns every note
        into a negotiation.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - data-engineering
          - domain-analysis
          - release-engineering
          - risk-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - write
        connectors:
          - mcp:mam
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n-approval
      kind: approval
      name: Director approves the reel for screening
      summary: Pause for the director; on timeout, escalate.
    - id: workflow-output
      kind: output
      name: Released deliverable
      summary: Return the completed Reel assembly + teacher critique deliverable, the evidence behind
        it, and every unresolved item.
  edges:
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-1
      from: n-intake
      to: n-scope
      kind: data
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-2
      from: n-scope
      to: n-segment1
      kind: data
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-3
      from: n-scope
      to: n-segment2
      kind: data
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-4
      from: n-scope
      to: n-segment3
      kind: data
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-5
      from: n-segment1
      to: n-assemble
      kind: data
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-6
      from: n-segment2
      to: n-assemble
      kind: data
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-7
      from: n-segment3
      to: n-assemble
      kind: data
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-8
      from: n-assemble
      to: n-critique
      kind: data
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-9
      from: n-critique
      to: n-quality
      kind: data
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-10
      from: n-quality
      to: n-accept
      kind: data
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-11
      from: n-accept
      to: n-approval
      kind: control
      condition: 'true'
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-12
      from: n-accept
      to: n-revise
      kind: control
      condition: 'false'
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-13
      from: n-revise
      to: n-approval
      kind: data
    - id: wf-film-02-edge-14
      from: n-approval
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
      condition: approved
